items.title: Supreme Court asks Calcutta HC to urgently decide plea on disqualification of rebel TMC MLAs
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday urged the Calcutta High Court to decide expeditiously a plea flagging the West Bengal Assembly Speaker's delay in deciding the disqualification petitions against 10 rebel Trinamool Congress (TMC) members of legislative assembly (MLAs). [Sobhandeb Chattopadhyay v. Speaker] A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi asked the Calcutta High Court Chief Justice to place the matter before a division bench for expeditious disposal. It ordered, "It seems to us that the petitioner has to take recourse to the Calcutta High Court. We accordingly dispose of this petition at this stage with liberty to the petitioner to file an appropriate petition before the High Court. We request the Chief Justice of the High Court to list the matter before a Division Bench for urgent consideration and decide the matter expeditiously." CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi The Court was hearing a fresh plea filed by TMC MLA Sobhandeb Chattopadhyay challenging the Speaker's delay. items.title: Former Supreme Court Justice Rajesh Bindal appointed NCLAT Chairperson
items.summary: Former Supreme Court Justice Rajesh Bindal has been appointed chairperson of the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT). Justice Bindal confirmed the development to Bar & Bench . Justice Bindal retired from the Supreme Court on April 15 this year after serving at the top court for over three years. He had earlier served as Chief Justice of the Allahabad High Court before his elevation to the Supreme Court in February 2023. The appointment comes months after former Supreme Court Justice Ashok Bhushan completed his tenure as NCLAT chairperson on July 4, 2026. Following Justice Bhushan's retirement, Justice Yogesh Khanna, a judicial member of the appellate tribunal, was appointed officiating chairperson from July 5. His tenure was subsequently extended by the Central government in October. The development also assumes significance against the backdrop of recent proceedings before the Supreme Court concerning the functioning of the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT). Justice Bindal's appointment places him at the helm of the appellate tribunal dealing with some of the country's most significant corporate insolvency, restructuring and competition law disputes. #BREAKING Forme

items.title: Lawyer can't sue client for defamation for ending professional engagement: Patna High Court
items.summary: The Patna High Court recently held that a lawyer cannot claim defamation merely because a client decides to discontinue their professional engagement, even if the decision results in financial loss or reputational consequences [SBI Vs Mantosh Prasad Sinha]. Justice Ramesh Chand Malviya made the observation while rejecting a ₹25 lakh defamation suit filed by an advocate against officials of the State Bank of India (SBI) after he was removed from the bank's panel. The Court emphasised that an advocate's right to practise law does not translate into a right to be engaged or retained by a particular client. " The right to practise is a right to appear when engaged; it is not a right to be engaged," the Court observed in its order of October 27. It further held that a client was free to change lawyers without having to justify the decision. " No law requires a client to give reasons for disengaging an advocate, and the exercise of that freedom, whether by withdrawing a vakalatnama, by engaging a fresh counsel or by removing an advocate from a panel, is the exercise of a legal right. It is not, of itself, an imputation upon the advocate ," the Court said. Patna High Court No law requires

items.title: Delhi High Court allows sale of book about Rana Kapoor after deletion of four offending passages
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Friday lifted the blanket ban on the sale and circulation of a book titled 'Yes Man: The Untold Story of Rana Kapoor' [Harper Collins Publishers India Pvt Ltd v Rana Kapoor & Ors] . Justice Harish Vaidyanathan Shankar ruled that the trial court's findings that four statements in the book were defamatory or derogatory could not justify the ban on the entire book. Therefore, the High Court modified the trial court's order and said that the injunction would apply only to those four passages. "The Impugned Order is accordingly modified to the extent that the restraint in respect of the Subject Book shall operate only against those portions thereof in which Statements (ii), (iv), (vii) and (x), as identified in the Impugned Order, occur. The remaining portions of the Subject Book shall not be covered by the injunction merely by reason of the findings returned in respect of the aforesaid statements," the Court said. items.title: Authorities can't pass orders blindly based on panel lawyer's legal opinion: Karnataka High Court
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently held that administrative and statutory authorities cannot pass executive orders blindly, relying solely the legal opinion of their panel advocates. Justice T M Nadaf held that legal opinions given by panel advocates are only advisory in nature and cannot replace the independent decision-making process of the competent authority. The Court added that an authority that merely copies or approves a legal opinion without examining the relevant facts and law abdicates its statutory power and acts under dictation. “ If an authority blindly copies or signs off the order only on the legal opinion, without examining the facts and relevant law by itself, it amounts to an abdication of statutory power and acting under dictation. Such orders require to be held as arbitrary, invalid and lacking jurisdiction ,” the Court said. . items.title: Unpaid traffic challans issued before October 2020 cannot be ground to deny vehicle registration: Kerala High Court
items.summary: The Kerala High Court has held that transport authorities cannot refuse to process applications relating to vehicle registration, merely because traffic challans issued before October 1, 2020, remain unpaid. [TN Kumar v Ministry of Road Transport and Highways & ors] Justice Murali Purushothaman held that Rule 167(7) of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 (Rules) as amended , which restricts certain vehicle-related services when traffic challans remain unpaid, cannot be applied to violations that occurred before the provision came into force. The Court explained that the rule introduced a restriction that did not previously exist and could therefore operate only from the date it came into force. It clarified that unless the law clearly provided otherwise, a new restriction could not be imposed on the basis of challans issued before the rule was introduced. items.summary: The Allahabad High Court on Thursday rejected a plea seeking the registration of a First Information Report (FIR) against Congress leader Rahul Gandhi in relation to the remarks made by him about religious freedom in India, in relation to the Sikh community [Nageshwar Mishra and another v State of UP and another] Justice Vikram D Chauhan noted that Gandhi had said that there is an atmosphere of insecurity among Sikhs in India. The Court observed that the statement only raised concerns about a community or section of society. Gandhi as an elected representative has the right to raise concerns in respect of a minority community, the bench added. "The respondent no. 2 being an elected representative has a right to raise concerns in respect of section of society. Further, questioning the rights of minorities by elected representative by itself cannot be an offence and the said speech of respondent no. 2 will have protection of freedom of speech and expression under Article 19 of Constitution," the Court said.
